articles.title: How to show Argo CD deployments on Jira work items
articles.excerpt: "Is this ticket in production yet?" is easy to answer when a pipeline deploys your code, because Jira's deployment view is filled by tools such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins and Azure DevOps. With GitOps…
articles.body: "Is this ticket in production yet?" is easy to answer when a pipeline deploys your code, because Jira's deployment view is filled by tools such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins and Azure DevOps. With GitOps it stays empty. Argo CD pulls the change into the cluster, so no pipeline step ever tells Jira that a deployment happened. This article shows how to close that gap yourself, using only Argo CD's built-in notifications and Jira's Deployments API. At the end there is a ready-made app, if you would rather not maintain the pieces. What you need Argo CD 2.3 or later. The notifications controller is included. Jira Cloud, with permission to create OAuth credentials or install an app. Commit messages that contain the work item key, for example KAN-12 raise the timeout .
articles.author: Jira apps

articles.title: Why can't I see the image Claude Code reads?
articles.excerpt: When Claude Code reads a screenshot, or its browser tool takes one, your terminal prints a line like Read 1 file. The picture goes to the model. You never see it. Codex draws a thumbnail too small to…
articles.body: When Claude Code reads a screenshot, or its browser tool takes one, your terminal prints a line like Read 1 file . The picture goes to the model. You never see it. Codex draws a thumbnail too small to read, and Grok prints one line with a file path. To check what the agent actually looked at: Open the file. If the image is on disk, run open <path> on macOS, or Cmd+Click the path in Codex and Grok. Ask for a file. Browser screenshots are not files until you ask. Tell Claude Code to save the screenshot to a path, then open that. Let the terminal draw it. Codex does this on Kitty or Sixel terminals. Claude Code can through a mod, in Ghostty, kitty, or iTerm2. Keep it beside the agent. PonyMux shows the pictures the agent receives in a floating Agent View over its Terminal.

articles.title: How Were 178 Websites Hacked? Who Was Behind the Optimizely Cyberattack and When Did It Happen?
articles.excerpt: How Were 178 Websites Hacked? Who Was Behind the Optimizely Cyberattack and When Did It Happen? A cyberattack involving Optimizely exposed visitors of websites associated with 178 organisations to mal…
articles.body: How Were 178 Websites Hacked? Who Was Behind the Optimizely Cyberattack and When Did It Happen? A cyberattack involving Optimizely exposed visitors of websites associated with 178 organisations to malicious code, including websites linked to CNN, BBC, Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA and HSBC. The attackers exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Web Experimentation, a platform businesses use to test website designs, personalise content and measure visitor behaviour. They inserted malicious JavaScript into customer projects, allowing the code to reach visitors through websites that relied on the service. The malware was designed to steal cryptocurrency, capture payment card details, collect browser cookies and screenshots, and deliver exploit kits targeting vulnerable iPhones and iPads.
articles.author: Anointed

articles.title: I kept rebooting my machine to run local LLMs, so I built canfit
articles.excerpt: The frustration While building my previous open-source project, Knemora, I was running local LLMs on my Mac alongside Docker, a browser with too many tabs and everything else a developer keeps open. M…
articles.body: The frustration While building my previous open-source project, Knemora , I was running local LLMs on my Mac alongside Docker, a browser with too many tabs and everything else a developer keeps open. Memory kept running out. Every time, the same question: what can I close safely, without killing something macOS needs? The classic top shows you numbers, not answers. It doesn't tell you whether the model you're about to load will fit, and it doesn't tell you which of those hundreds of processes are safe to close. More than once I just gave up and rebooted . So I built the tool I wanted. Meet canfit canfit is the top command for people running local LLMs and apps. It tells you if a model or an app can launch right now and, if it can't, what you can safely close to make room.

articles.title: Microsoft Foundry: Is Deploy as Web App Enough, or Do You Need a Backend Proxy?
articles.excerpt: I used AI tools to help draft and edit this post. I checked the facts and the wording, and the original lives at geekindata.com. The diagrams are on that page. Key takeaways Treat a Foundry webapp as…
articles.body: I used AI tools to help draft and edit this post. I checked the facts and the wording, and the original lives at geekindata.com . The diagrams are on that page. Identity and egress first; the container is table stakes Key takeaways Treat a Foundry webapp as identity and egress design that happens to run a container. Reuse one Entra and managed-identity plane; do not invent parallel registrations without a map. Separate ingress product decisions from VNet integration and private egress. Secretless OBO needs the right user-assigned identity, audience, and API permissions. Plan private endpoints and private DNS from the App Service subnet outward. Gate releases on identity and DNS before prompt evals or Node tuning. Teams still celebrate when the container listens on the right port.

articles.title: We Wrote 66 Zero-Dependency Python Physics Verifiers to Model Brewing Steak from CO2, Sunlight & 4.20 MHz Ultrasound — Prove Our Math Wrong
articles.excerpt: Why did $2 billion+ in venture-backed cultivated animal meat hit a thermodynamic and unit-economics wall? Because mammalian cells were never meant to be grown in $500/L recombinant growth factors insi…
articles.body: Why did $2 billion+ in venture-backed cultivated animal meat hit a thermodynamic and unit-economics wall? Because mammalian cells were never meant to be grown in $500/L recombinant growth factors inside pharmaceutical-grade stirred-tank bioreactors with a 36-hour doubling time. For the past several months, we took a completely different, software-first systems engineering approach ( Project MANNA , 100% public domain under CC0 1.0 ): we wrote 66 zero-dependency Python 3 physics, electrochemistry, bioprocess, and acoustics verifiers to model whether you can bypass both the cow and mammalian cell culture entirely—converting captured $\text{CO}_2$, sunlight, and water into whole-cut steak, poultry, or fish fillets for $0.84/lb dry (~$1.10/lb hydrated fillet) .

articles.title: NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how
articles.excerpt: NASA invites the public to shine lights in Morse code after sunset today (Nov. 17) to celebrate Voyager 1 reaching a historic distance of one light-day from Earth.
articles.body: As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft. The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth . And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency.

articles.excerpt: It was a spectacle many regard as the greatest meteor display on record.
articles.body: Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories.

articles.title: Reflect Orbital wants to launch thousands of sunlight-beaming mirrors to space — and the 1st will go up next year
articles.excerpt: Reflect Orbital is moving forward with its ambitious plan to place thousands of mirrors in Earth orbit and sell redirected sunlight after dark.
articles.body: Reflect Orbital is moving forward with its plan to place mirrors in Earth orbit to produce and sell sunlight after dark. The goal is to extend the hours and output of solar farms globally, "making clean power dispatchable and available when you need it," the California-based startup explains on its website . Reflect Orbital has made significant progress to date. On Tuesday (Nov. 10), for example, the company announced it had secured $73.5 million in new funding, boosting its total raise to more than $100 million. It has also gotten a formal go-ahead from the U.S. government to try out the concept in space and is currently readying its first test satellite , which is expected to launch in the second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns
articles.excerpt: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
articles.body: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak.
